definition: A called shot is a dated, public, falsifiable statement about something the subject is about to do or find out — filed before the outcome is known, with a named resolution date and a verdict printed on that date whether it was hit or missed. A miss is rendered exactly like a hit. The calendar adjudicates; nothing here is a performance claim and no figure in this file is a claim.

shots.thesis: A publicly funded programme creates value only when the people it was built for get from awareness to completion, and the outreach, intake, follow-up, scheduling and reporting between those two points are usually fragmented. The thesis under validation: that participant-operations infrastructure is a repeatable category rather than a one-off pattern, and that the right way in is as a partner beneath an established programme operator — never as a prime.
shots.will_have_done: Established, for one live programme, the procurement mechanism, the buyer class and a safe pilot shape — or published here that I could not.
boundaries: Exploratory. Nothing has shipped, nothing is claimed, no partner or programme is named.
Meta paid social remains the only owned channel specialism on this site; this lane claims none.
